content.value_statement: Linux hosting setup can lock users out or expose services when steps are rushed. This skill guides ordered SSH, firewall, Nginx, DNS, and TLS changes with validation gates.
actual_capabilities: Routes advice by Linux distro family before package or service commands are suggested.
Separates static-site hosting from Nginx reverse-proxy hosting workflows.
Orders SSH hardening steps to reduce lockout risk.
Guides firewall exposure with a deny-by-default inbound posture.
Checks HTTPS readiness before certificate issuance and redirects.
Defers BBR and kernel tuning until secure hosting is stable.
limitations: It does not design Kubernetes, PaaS, or container orchestration deployments.
It does not cover Windows or macOS host administration.
It requires current official documentation for exact distro commands.
It is not a full SRE review for complex multi-tenant production platforms.

use_cases.title: Launch a personal site
use_cases.description: Plan a safe first setup for DNS, Nginx, SSH, firewall rules, and HTTPS on a new Linux VPS.

use_cases.title: Review a small server
use_cases.description: Check whether SSH, firewall exposure, Nginx routing, and TLS sequencing follow safe operational order.

use_cases.title: Troubleshoot a proxy rollout
use_cases.description: Separate app health, loopback binding, Nginx configuration, DNS, and certificate issues during deployment.

prompt_templates.title: Start a safe VPS setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me set up a new Linux VPS for a website. Ask what you need first, then give the safest phase sequence.

prompt_templates.title: Harden SSH and firewall
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my SSH and firewall plan for a Linux web server. Focus on lockout risk and public port exposure.

prompt_templates.title: Configure Nginx hosting branch
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me choose between static Nginx hosting and a reverse proxy. I will share my app type, domain, and distro.

prompt_templates.title: Audit TLS rollout order
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit my HTTPS rollout sequence for DNS, HTTP validation, certificate issuance, renewal, redirects, and failure recovery.

output_examples.input: I have a new Ubuntu VPS and want to host a static website.
output: A brief intake checklist for distro, access, DNS, and hosting goal.
A safe phase order covering access, firewall, Nginx, HTTP validation, HTTPS, and final checks.
A short failure branch for common DNS, permissions, and Nginx mistakes.

output_examples.input: My app works locally, but the public domain fails through Nginx.
output: A troubleshooting path that checks app health before Nginx proxy settings.
A separation of local server checks and remote browser or DNS checks.
A likely cause list for loopback binding, service state, firewall, policy, and certificate issues.

output_examples.input: Can I enable HTTPS redirects now?
output: A readiness review for DNS, HTTP response, certificate installation, domain match, and browser warnings.
A recommendation to delay redirects until HTTPS is confirmed working.
A validation plan for final HTTP and HTTPS behavior.

best_practices: Verify distro-specific package names, service units, and config paths before giving commands.
Keep a second SSH session or recovery path before changing authentication rules.
Validate each phase before moving to the next risky hosting change.
anti_patterns: Do not disable SSH password or root login from the only active session.
Do not expose backend application ports publicly when Nginx can proxy loopback.
Do not force HTTP-to-HTTPS redirects before HTTPS is proven healthy.

faq.question: Does this skill give exact commands for every Linux distro?
faq.answer: No. It routes by distro family and expects current official documentation before exact commands are used.

faq.question: Can it help with both static sites and app proxies?
faq.answer: Yes. It keeps those branches separate so users receive the correct Nginx pattern.

faq.question: Does it include HTTPS guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers certificate readiness, ACME client choice, renewal posture, and redirect timing.

faq.question: Is it suitable for Kubernetes deployments?
faq.answer: No. It is focused on direct Linux server hosting with Nginx, SSH, firewalls, and TLS.

faq.question: How does it reduce lockout risk?
faq.answer: It requires a working key login, second session, or recovery path before risky SSH changes.

faq.answer: Yes. The metadata declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
